_what: Raw MCP JSON-RPC exchange with the claims-system server over stdio, captured byte-for-byte by week9/wire_capture.py (raw lines in week9/wire_raw.jsonl). 'raw' is the exact line on the pipe; 'message' is the same line parsed; 'annotations' covers every top-level field, written by hand.
_transport: stdio: the host spawns the server as a child process; client->server messages go on its stdin, server->client on its stdout, one JSON object per line. stderr is free for logs.
model_call: No model call happens anywhere in this exchange or inside either server. The model runs only in the host (app/mcphost/agent.py run_query -> app.llm.chat_with_tools), after tools/list has told it what exists and before tools/call carries the call it chose.

annotations.jsonrpc: Always the string "2.0": this is JSON-RPC 2.0, the envelope MCP is built on.
annotations.id: 1, chosen by the client. The server must echo it so the reply can be matched to this request. A message with an id is a request and must get exactly one response.
annotations.method: "initialize": always the first message on a new connection. Nothing else may be sent before it.
annotations.params: The client's offer. protocolVersion = the newest spec revision the client speaks (2025-11-25). capabilities = {} because this raw client offers nothing back (no sampling, no roots, no elicitation). clientInfo = who is connecting, which the server can log.

annotations.id: 1, echoing the request's id. This is the answer to step 1.
annotations.result: The server's half of the handshake. protocolVersion = the revision it agreed to (it accepted 2025-11-25). capabilities = what it serves: tools (listChanged false, so the tool list won't change mid-session), plus empty prompts/resources blocks that FastMCP always advertises. serverInfo = name "claims-system"; the version 1.30.0 is the SDK's default, not the vendor's 0.4.1, so the server doesn't actually identify its own build (a point for the risk note).

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized": the client confirms the handshake is done. Only after this may normal requests flow.
annotations.(no id): No id field means this is a NOTIFICATION, so the server sends no reply. That's why there's no server line between steps 3 and 4.

annotations.id: 2: a new id for a new request.
annotations.method: "tools/list": discovery. The host asks what the server can do instead of having it hard-coded. app/mcphost/agent.py builds its whole tool list from this reply.
annotations.(no params): params omitted, so this is the first page. A cursor would go here to fetch the next page if the reply carried nextCursor.

exchange.raw:
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"name":"get_claim_status","description":"Current status of one claim: policy number and line, status, date of loss,
    reported loss type, claimed amount, policy excess, assigned adjuster and the
    date it was last updated. claim_number looks like CLM-2026-10002.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"title":"get_claim_statusArguments","type":"object"}},{"name":"get_adjuster_notes","description":"Full adjuster note history for one claim, oldest first: each entry has a
    date, an author (adjuster id or intake) and the note text verbatim.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"claim_number":{"title":"Claim Number","type":"string"}},"required":["claim_number"],"title":"get_adjuster_notesArguments","type":"object"}}]}}

tools.name: get_claim_status
tools.description:
Current status of one claim: policy number and line, status, date of loss,
    reported loss type, claimed amount, policy excess, assigned adjuster and the
    date it was last updated. claim_number looks like CLM-2026-10002.

tools.name: get_adjuster_notes
tools.description:
Full adjuster note history for one claim, oldest first: each entry has a
    date, an author (adjuster id or intake) and the note text verbatim.

annotations.result: tools[] holds 2 entries. Each has: name (what the model will call; the host prefixes it to claims-system__get_claim_status); description (the function's docstring, shipped verbatim, which is the only guidance the model gets about when and how to call it, so it's a PROMPT); inputSchema (the JSON Schema generated from the Python signature: one required string claim_number). No nextCursor, so this is the complete list. 2 tools, the number reported in tool_counts.md.

annotations.method: "tools/call": run one tool. In the agent, this message is built from the tool_use block the MODEL emitted. Here it's sent by hand, with no model involved.
annotations.params: name = the tool's own name as tools/list gave it ("get_claim_status", without the host's "claims-system__" prefix, which the host strips before routing). arguments = an object that must satisfy that tool's inputSchema.

annotations.result: content[] holds one text block, the claim status record serialised as JSON text. This is what the host puts into the model's tool_result. isError = false: the tool ran and found the claim. A tool failure (e.g. unknown claim) comes back HERE, as result.isError = true with the message as text, so the model can read it and recover. A JSON-RPC top-level "error" object is reserved for protocol failures (unknown method, malformed request), which the model never sees as a tool result.
